season.evidence: Only 32 logged ascents, spread Feb-Oct with the summer months fullest (Jun 6, Jul 5, Sep 5, Aug 3, Oct 3); the two harvested tracks are winter snowshoe trips. No guidebook or agency page found for this unofficial peak, so low confidence.

otherTracksConsidered.why: 7 Apr 2024, snowshoes, rope and a 20 ft ice step; winter.
4 Sep 2020 in season, but a camp-based scramble from the Tamarack Meadows lake with no track points and no logged route.

pins.name: Snow Lakes Trailhead
pins.evidence: Both winter tracks and the Apr 2024 track start within about 20 m of this spot, and the Mountaineers report for the climb starts at the Snow Lakes trailhead and goes via Nada Lake. The route has no trailhead pin. Tracks are off-season, so they only nominate the location.
pins.confirmedBy: https://www.wta.org/go-hiking/hikes/snow-lakes (WTA hike page lists Snow Lakes Trailhead at 47.5441, -120.7097, Icicle Creek Road)

pins.name: Three Musketeers Ridge
pins.evidence: Route has no summit pin. Peakbagger's surveyed summit (lidar, 7690 ft) is 7 m from the highest point of one track and 19 m from the other.
pins.confirmedBy: Peakbagger peak 21423 surveyed coordinate plus tracks 1342400 and 1342576

facts.text: One early-September party camped at the unnamed lake in Tamarack Meadows and reached the ridge saddle by climbing steep but easy ground from the end of the lake; the slopes are hot and shadeless, so carry plenty of water.
From the saddle the high point is a scramble over a series of knobs, with a few boulder moves including a slot.

notes: The route is an empty shell (no grade, text, season or pins) and is filed under id wa_big_chiwaukum_three_musketeers_ridge; it may have been created under Big Chiwaukum. The only in-season report approaches from the Tamarack Meadows side (after climbing The Temple), while the winter tracks come from Snow Lakes trailhead via Nada Lake; the pin add assumes the Snow Lakes approach is the primary one, and both pin adds are optional if the owner prefers the other. A winter report states that in summer the basin above Nada Lake is reached by small ledges and slabs rather than a gully; it was not used because it is an off-season report. Season is low confidence.
